title: Kinetic Friction
theory:
**Big idea:** When surfaces slide over each other, friction opposes the **sliding** (the relative motion). Its size is μ_k times the normal force.

**(a) Direction**
The kinetic friction on body A sliding against body B is **opposite to the velocity of A relative to B**. The velocity that matters is relative to the body **applying** the friction.

**Example: a block slipping on a moving box**
A long box on wheels moves right along a road. A small block on it slips back and falls off the rear end. Seen from the road, both move right, but the block moves slower.
- Relative to the box, the block moves **left**.
- So the friction on the block is **to the right**, and the friction on the box is to the left.

**(b) Magnitude**
**f_k = μ_k N**
- μ_k = **coefficient of kinetic friction**. It depends on the two materials and how rough their surfaces are, and it has no units.
- It is **independent of the speed** (approximately, for speeds below about 10 m/s).
- It is **independent of the area of contact** for the same N. A slab slid flat or standing on its narrow face feels the same friction.

**🧮 Worked example:** a 20 kg box is pulled along a horizontal floor, with μ_k = 0.25.
- N = Mg, so f_k = 0.25 × 20 × 9.8 = **49 N**, opposite to the pull.

**🧮 Worked example:** a 10 kg block is pulled by a 50 N horizontal force, with μ_k = 0.3 and g = 10 m/s².
- f_k = 0.3 × 100 = 30 N, so the net force is 20 N and **a = 2 m/s²**.

> ⚠️ **Common mistake:** Taking friction opposite to the velocity measured from the ground. Use the velocity **relative to the surface** that exerts the friction.

questions.prompt: The magnitude of kinetic friction is given by:
questions.explanation: Kinetic friction is proportional to the normal force: f_k = μ_k N.

questions.prompt: The kinetic friction on a body A sliding on a body B acts:

options.text: Opposite to the velocity of A relative to B
Opposite to the velocity of A relative to the ground

questions.explanation: It opposes the motion relative to the body that applies the friction.

questions.prompt: A 20 kg box is pulled along a horizontal floor (μ_k = 0.25, g = 9.8 m/s²). The force of kinetic friction on it is:
For the same normal force, if the area of contact between two sliding surfaces is doubled, the kinetic friction:
questions.explanation: Friction depends on N, not on the area of contact.

questions.prompt: A 10 kg block is pulled by a 50 N horizontal force on a floor with μ_k = 0.3 (g = 10 m/s²). Its acceleration is:
A block slips backward on a moving truck and both move forward relative to the road, the block more slowly. The friction on the block from the truck acts:
questions.explanation: Relative to the truck the block moves backward, so friction on it points forward.

questions.prompt: The coefficient of kinetic friction depends mainly on:

options.text: The nature (materials and roughness) of the two surfaces

questions.explanation: μ_k depends on the two materials and their roughness, not on speed (roughly), area or mass.
